reasons: Mostly definitions, so there is little to test here.
The checks themselves live in verifier.ts, and no test is visible in this packet.

terms.meaning: a rulebook that checks data has the right shape at run time
a label pointing to where a fact came from
an optional score from 0 to 1 that the model may attach to a claim
one statement of analysis with a kind and its sources

sections.name: File setup, CLAIM_KINDS, ClaimKind
sections.title: Allowed claim kinds
sections.what: Lists the four kinds a claim can have: OBSERVED, DERIVED, MODEL_ESTIMATE and EDITORIAL. Every claim must name one.
sections.why: The file header says every generated item is a list of typed, sourced claims.
sections.watch_out: The verifier only demands source ids for OBSERVED and DERIVED, so the kind decides how strictly a claim is checked.

sections.name: claimSchema, Claim, claimsSchema, Claims
sections.title: Claim and claim list format
sections.what: Defines one claim: text up to 400 characters, a kind, up to 12 source ids, and an optional confidence from 0 to 1. A list must hold between 1 and 8 claims, and extra fields are refused.
sections.why: Likely reason: small, predictable output makes bad output fail early.
sections.watch_out: These limits are real rules, so model output that goes past them fails before the verifier even runs.

sections.name: Fact
sections.title: Fact handed to the generator
sections.what: Describes one fact the model may quote: an id, a value (number or text), its source id, when it was observed, and its kind. Editorial is not a valid kind for a fact.
sections.why: Likely reason: facts are the only material the model may quote, so their shape is fixed.
sections.watch_out: The value is the only text or number a claim may repeat, and a fact with a wrong observed time can slip past or be wrongly blocked by the cutoff check.

summary: Defines the shape of generated analysis: typed claims with sources, and the verified facts the model is allowed to quote.
purpose: Give the model and the checker one agreed format.
why: The file header says it implements the generation contract in the design document it names.
how: 1) The model must return output matching the claims schema. 2) Each claim is then checked against the facts by the verifier. 3) Facts are the only material handed to the model.
inputs: Model output in JSON form, and facts prepared by the calling code.
outputs: Parsed and shape-checked claim lists, or an error when the shape is wrong.
risks: Changing limits or kinds can break stored output and the prompt text that describes them.
debug: If model output fails at parsing, compare its fields and sizes with the limits here. If a fact is rejected, check its kind and observed time.
